lead: UN Secretary-General António Guterres used his Islamabad visit to endorse Pakistan's mediation between Washington and Tehran, even as US Vice President JD Vance made a sharp cut in Iranian enrichment the price of ending the war. Pakistan tested an extended-range Fatah-4 cruise missile, the defence minister said Pakistani forces were giving reconnaissance support to Saudi operations against the Houthis, and Ishaq Dar warned that denying Pakistan its Indus waters would threaten regional security. At home, gunmen killed five people in Dera Ismail Khan as the government made further talks conditional on the PTI ending its march, while an IMF staff mission appeared set to clear about $1.2bn and the KSE-100 recovered strongly.

stories.headline: Guterres backs Pakistan's US–Iran mediation, urges return to diplomacy
stories.summary: At a press conference with Ishaq Dar in Islamabad, the UN Secretary-General praised Pakistan's central role in mediating between the US and Iran and called on both sides to end the conflict and restore freedom of navigation in the Gulf. President Zardari conferred the Nishan-e-Imtiaz on Guterres during the visit.

stories.headline: Vance says Iran must sharply cut enrichment to end war
stories.summary: In a Reuters interview carried by Business Recorder, US Vice President JD Vance said Tehran must make a meaningful reduction in its enrichment capacity to end the seven-month war, while admitting Washington was unsure how Iran reaches decisions in negotiations. The demand sets a high bar for the Pakistan-brokered track.

stories.headline: Poland and Uzbekistan seek deeper economic ties with Islamabad
stories.summary: Visiting Polish minister Tomasz Siemoniak praised Pakistan's regional role and said Warsaw wanted stronger economic cooperation, while Uzbekistan's ambassador discussed industrial, trade and investment links under the two countries' February 2026 agreement.

stories.headline: Gunmen kill five in two Dera Ismail Khan attacks
stories.summary: Unidentified attackers opened fire on a Federal Board of Revenue enforcement squad and, separately, on a highway traffic police vehicle in Dera Ismail Khan, killing five people, police said; outlets differ on how many of the dead were officials. Express Tribune also reported two militants killed in a gunfight in Bannu and three people abducted in Tank.

stories.headline: Five militants killed in North Waziristan operation, officials say
stories.summary: Security forces killed five militants and wounded two in an intelligence-based operation in North Waziristan, according to security sources quoted by state media, which described them as members of the group the state calls Fitna al-Khawarij.

stories.headline: Government ties PTI talks to ending march and counterterrorism backing
stories.summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif said talks could resume only if the PTI called off its march on Islamabad, warning that blockades threatened economic gains, while Minister of State Talal Chaudhry accused Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's chief minister of derailing negotiations and demanded the province's full support for counterterrorism action. The PTI dismissed the offer as symbolic.

stories.headline: Pakistan tests extended-range Fatah-4 cruise missile
stories.summary: ISPR said the army carried out a successful test of an extended-range version of the indigenous, ground-launched Fatah-4 cruise missile, which it said had improved accuracy and upgraded avionics and navigation. The system belongs to the Army Rocket Force Command.

stories.headline: Asif says Pakistani forces aid Saudi anti-Houthi reconnaissance
stories.summary: Defence Minister Khawaja Asif said Pakistani and Turkish forces were supporting Saudi Arabia's operations against the Houthis in Yemen with reconnaissance, describing the role as defensive. Al Jazeera noted that Riyadh's offensive tests how long Islamabad can stay out of combat; on Monday the information ministry dismissed a Reuters report on the Makkah pact as speculative.

stories.headline: PM orders winter gas plan to keep imports flowing
stories.summary: Shehbaz Sharif told officials to draw up a gas load-management plan for winter and take steps to guarantee uninterrupted gas imports, citing the regional situation as the Gulf conflict threatens LNG supply.

stories.headline: Fuel subsidy reaches over nine million low-income people
stories.summary: Officials said targeted fuel support had reached more than nine million low-income people as the US–Iran war keeps petrol and diesel prices high and feeds through to transport and food costs.

stories.headline: IRSA sets 22 per cent water shortfall for rabi crops
stories.summary: The Indus River System Authority's advisory committee approved a 22 per cent water shortage for both Punjab and Sindh for the October–March rabi season, a squeeze on wheat sowing.

stories.headline: Trade gap widens as exports slow and imports climb
stories.summary: Business Recorder reported that export growth is losing momentum while imports keep rising sharply, pushing the trade deficit wider and adding pressure on the external account.

stories.headline: IMF mission talks on track to unlock about $1.2bn
stories.summary: Talks with the visiting IMF staff mission were expected to end positively this week, Dawn reported, opening the way to roughly $1.2bn under the fourth review of the $7bn Extended Fund Facility and the third review of the $1.4bn Resilience and Sustainability Facility, subject to board approval.

stories.headline: KSE-100 rebounds 2,593 points on talks offer
stories.summary: The PSX benchmark recovered most of the previous session's losses as the prime minister's offer of dialogue with the PTI eased political worries and broad-based buying returned.

stories.headline: Bond yields near 13 per cent as rate-hike bets build
stories.summary: With the next monetary policy decision about two weeks away, secondary-market yields are rising, with 10-year bonds near 13 per cent against an 11.5 per cent policy rate, as bank treasuries increasingly price in a hike, Business Recorder noted.

stories.headline: Pakistan pitches $26bn in UNDP-backed projects to investors
stories.summary: The government sought $26bn of investment in 35 projects prepared with UNDP support and aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals; separately, Pakistan and the IFC advanced plans for a fund to back start-ups.

stories.headline: Dar warns Indus water denial threatens regional security
stories.summary: Speaking at a water symposium in Vienna, Ishaq Dar said any attempt to deprive Pakistan of its share under the Indus Waters Treaty would have serious consequences for regional peace, while Pakistan's delegation at the UN Human Rights Council accused India of using water as a tool of coercion.

stories.headline: PTI march camps at Mattani, turns towards Khyber
stories.summary: The PTI convoy led by Chief Minister Sohail Afridi stopped overnight at Mattani outside Peshawar and is heading to Khyber district next.

stories.headline: Imran Khan's cousin detained for 30 days
stories.summary: Qasim Zaman was taken into custody at Adiala jail under a public-order detention order issued by the Rawalpindi deputy commissioner, the PTI said.

stories.headline: Punjab extends gatherings ban to 15 October
stories.summary: The provincial government renewed Section 144 for ten more days, citing threats of terrorist activity.

stories.headline: PTI threatens to quit assemblies over any KP governor's rule
stories.summary: The PTI said it would resign from the assemblies if governor's rule were imposed in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
